mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the same month indicates weakening consumer demand and housing market distress, which causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST < previous month * 0.90 in same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate profit margins, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% coincident with a decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 3% in the same month indicates supply-side contraction and weak demand, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month * 0.99 AND RSAFS < previous month * 0.97 in same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in the federal funds rate below 2% signals an emergency monetary easing in response to a financial crisis, which boosts risk appetite and equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops by >1.5pp in a single month to below 2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered crisis episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 1% month-over-month alongside a concurrent decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as profit margins compress.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month * 1.01 AND UNRATE < 4.0% in same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above 0.5% for four consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which supports corporate earnings and justifies higher equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of quarters where the condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline of more than 2% in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates a broad-based contraction in supply and construction activity, which negatively impacts corporate revenues and confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month * 0.98 AND HOUST < previous month * 0.98 in same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered months.
